This is government-reported information, not independent technical confirmation of attribution or Russian state direction. column2: DynoWiper update: Technical analysis and attribution
column13: Established cybersecurity research team with direct endpoint detection and malware-analysis observations; historical reporting accuracy has not been systematically audited and attribution relies partly on behavioural comparison, so Grade B remains provisional.
column14: ESET press release and detailed technical report originate from the same research organisation and are not independent corroboration; the report references CERT Polska SRC-006; overlap in investigated incident components and underlying evidence requires claim-level comparison.
column15: Original detailed technical article reviewed by analyst on 2026-10-13; underlying victim telemetry, complete incident-response records, initial-access evidence and full sample provenance are not independently available.
column16: ESET reports three DynoWiper variants deployed on 29 December 2025 against a Polish energy company and blocked by ESET PROTECT; describes file-wiping functionality, attempted credential access, proxy tooling and deployment via Group Policy-related mechanisms. ESET attributes the destructive malware component to Sandworm with medium confidence, citing similarities to ZOV and previous operations, while acknowledging no visibility into initial access and possible collaboration with another actor. The reported attribution is ESET\'s assessment, not an independent project finding. Subsequent comparison with CERT Polska SRC-006 establishes High analytical confidence that the DynoWiper reporting corresponds to the destructive-malware activity recorded as INC-003, supported by matching malware hashes and operational details. This technical correspondence does not resolve the differing actor-attribution assessments: ESET attributes the DynoWiper component to Sandworm with medium confidence, while CERT Polska associates the wider coordinated operation with the Static Tundra activity cluster.

Dragos notes historical technical and operational overlap between ELECTRUM and Sandworm. The public article most directly relates to INC-002; mapping to individual CHP incidents remains unconfirmed. The ELECTRUM attribution is Dragos assessment rather than an independently established project finding.

column15: Full text supplied and reviewed on 2026-10-13. Report states updated January 2026 without a verified exact publication day; the publication_date field uses 2026-01-28 provisionally based on the associated Dragos public article, not an independently verified brief publication date. The document bears a Proprietary & Confidential marking; do not reproduce or redistribute its contents. column16: Dragos reports involvement in incident response at one site affected by the 29 December 2025 Polish distributed-energy attacks and attributes the wider operation to ELECTRUM with moderate confidence. It describes disabled communications and OT equipment, acknowledges inadequate logging to determine whether operational commands were attempted, and discusses historical overlap between ELECTRUM and Sandworm without treating their classifications as identical. Dragos separately assesses opportunistic attacker behaviour with moderate confidence and incomplete preparation with low confidence. The report most directly informs INC-002; it does not independently establish ELECTRUM responsibility across all affected sites or a specific Russian state organisation.
